business_scope.primary_industry_name: Manufacture of Portable Phased-Array Medical Diagnostic Scanners

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Luxembourg (unitary national jurisdiction; no sub-state corporate tax distinction)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Agreement between the Government of the People's Republic of China and the Government of the Grand Duchy of Luxembourg on the Reciprocal Promotion and Protection of Investments (signed 11 May 1979, in force 1 June 1980)

Convention between Luxembourg and the People's Republic of China for the Avoidance of Double Taxation and the Prevention of Fiscal Evasion with respect to Taxes on Income and Capital (signed 12 March 1994, in force 14 April 1995, as amended by the Protocol of 16 July 2019)
EU-China Comprehensive Agreement on Investment (negotiated in 2020; ratification pending)
Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union (TFEU) provisions on freedom of establishment and free movement of capital
Convention on the Recognition and Enforcement of Foreign Arbitral Awards (New York 1958), applicable to both Luxembourg and the People's Republic of China

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing, as amended; Law of 10 August 1915 on commercial companies, as amended (LSC), including the SCSp regime introduced by the Law of 23 July 2016; Law of 13 January 2019 establishing the Register of Beneficial Owners, as amended; Law of 19 December 2002 on the register of commerce and companies and on the accounting and annual accounts of undertakings, as amended; CSSF Regulation No 12-02 of 14 December 2012 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing, as amended; Grand-Ducal Regulation of 23 September 2020 on the organization of the RCS.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Private_Internal (SCSp-specific restricted-access RBE regime: beneficial ownership data is filed with the Luxembourg Business Registers but is not accessible to the general public; access is granted to the Luxembourg tax authorities, the CSSF, the Financial Intelligence Unit and other competent authorities, as well as to regulated professionals subject to AML/CFT obligations on a justified request basis; general public access is excluded following CJEU jurisprudence and the SCSp restricted-access provisions)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of incorporation / valid business licence of the Chinese corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) of the People's Republic of China / local Market Supervision Administration
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the PRC (China accession to the Hague Apostille Convention effective 7 November 2023)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / corporate registry excerpt of the Chinese shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: SAMR registry / National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System of the PRC
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Chinese notarization followed by Hague Apostille

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board resolution of the Chinese shareholder authorizing the incorporation of the SCSp, designation of the general partner and appointment of authorised representatives
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of directors / shareholders' meeting of the Chinese corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Chinese notarization followed by Hague Apostille

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of attorney in favor of the Luxembourg authorised manager / domiciliation agent / law firm
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Chinese notarization followed by Hague Apostille

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarised passport copies and proof of residential address of each UBO and general partner representative
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Public Security Bureau / National Immigration Administration of the PRC and the Chinese notary office
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Chinese notarization followed by Hague Apostille

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter and source-of-funds statement for the initial contribution or anticipated financing
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Bank of the Chinese shareholder or the Luxembourg bank designated for the SCSp account
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization if required by the receiving Luxembourg credit institution; otherwise bank-stamped original under CSSF KYC rules

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: ISO 13485 quality-management certificate and/or CE / NMPA medical device registration certificate for the portable phased-array color Doppler ultrasound console
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notified body (e.g., TÜV Rheinland) or the National Medical Products Administration (NMPA) of the PRC
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Certified copy with Hague Apostille (conditional document for business-scope consistency and future licensing; not an RCS filing requirement)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, general partners, directors, authorised managers and beneficial owners against (i) the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List (EEAS), (ii) the UN Security Council Consolidated Sanctions List, (iii) OFAC SDN and non-SDN lists, (iv) the Luxembourg sanctions listings maintained by the Ministry of Foreign and European Affairs, (v) FATF public statements and high-risk jurisdiction lists, and (vi) reputable PEP databases (World-Check or equivalent). PEP status assessment and enhanced due diligence covering source of wealth and source of funds are required for foreign and domestic PEPs under Articles 4 and 5 of the amended Law of 12 November 2004 and CSSF Regulation 12-02. The screening must be repeated on a risk-sensitive, continuous basis during the life of the SCSp and fully documented for the Luxembourg FIU and the CSSF.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), online portal www.lbr.lu with e-RCS and name-reservation module; official public procedures access also via guichet.lu
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The SCSp name must contain, immediately before or after the chosen name, the statutory denomination 'Société en commandite spéciale' or the abbreviation 'SCSp'. The corporate name must be expressed in Latin script; Chinese characters are not registrable, and a Latin-script transliteration or an English/French name must be adopted. No mandatory national language rule applies to SCSp names, but the limited partnership agreement and public filings are normally prepared in English or French, with the RCS registration form completed in French.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Sovereign or royal designations: 'Luxembourg', 'État', 'Grand-Duché', 'Commune', 'royal', 'duché' (require prior ministerial or municipal authorization)

Financial-sector reserved terms: 'banque', 'bank', 'crédit', 'credit', 'assurance', 'insurance', 'réassurance', 'reinsurance', 'bourse', 'stock exchange', 'fonds d'investissement', 'investment fund', 'OPCVM', 'UCI', 'trust' (require prior CSSF or Ministry of Finance licence/authorization)
Legal-form misnomers: 'SA', 'S.A.', 'SARL', 'S.à r.l.', 'SCA', 'SECA', 'AG', 'GmbH', 'association sans but lucratif' (a.s.b.l.) or any other suffix falsely implying a different corporate form
Misleading profession or object descriptors misstating the medical-device manufacturing or export activity, such as 'bank', 'clinic' or 'hospital', without the required health-sector approvals
Names contrary to public order, good morals or Luxembourg sovereignty, and names that cannot be distinguished from an already registered or reserved name
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant or its counsel shall: (1) obtain the written refusal grounds from the RCS/LBR; (2) where feasible, file an amended name-reservation request; (3) if the amended name is again refused, submit a reasoned re-examination request to the Luxembourg Business Registers service within one month of the refusal; (4) if no redress is granted, introduce an urgent petition (requête) before the President of the Tribunal d'arrondissement de Luxembourg (commercial chamber), under Article 33 of the amended Law of 19 December 2002, seeking a judicial order requiring registration of the name; (5) appeal any adverse judicial decision to the Court of Appeal of Luxembourg within the statutory time limits, generally one month for commercial matters. The incorporation deed should be kept in draft during the appeal so that the 60-day reservation window and the statutory publication sequence are not exceeded.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Conditional: an SCSp may maintain its registered office at the address of a licensed corporate domiciliation agent in Luxembourg under the amended Law of 31 May 1999 on the domiciliation of companies. However, a purely virtual office without an authorised local manager, local accounting records, a Luxembourg bank account and demonstrable decision-making substance is not acceptable for a commercial medical-imaging exporter. A licensed domiciliation agent is workable for the registered-office seat, but the SCSp must maintain a local general partner and economic substance in Luxembourg to avoid rebuttal of the Luxembourg seat and to preserve pass-through eligibility.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low quantified risk: approximately 8% per annum in the first two full financial years. Unannounced physical inspections by the RCS, the Luxembourg tax administration (Administration des contributions directes) or the CSSF for AML/CFT compliance are possible but statistically limited for a Low_Risk_Standard, non-financial partnership with no walk-in customers; the risk increases in case of UBO disclosure irregularities, use of a low-quality domiciliation provider or adverse sanctions-screen findings.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: RCS/LBR name clearance and name-reservation fee (single reservation, 60 days)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory LBR tariff (Grand-Ducal Regulation of 23 September 2020 on the RCS)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Luxembourg notarial fee for the SCSp incorporation deed / formalisation of the limited partnership agreement
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory notarial tariff and prevailing market benchmark for cross-border partnership deeds

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified translation of Chinese constitutional documents, business licence, board resolution and passports into French/English
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing official-certified translation market tariff in Luxembourg

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Chinese notarization and Hague Apostille processing for corporate documents and UBO identity files
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: PRC notary office and Ministry of Foreign Affairs (Consular Department) / provincial foreign affairs offices
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory Chinese notarization and apostille fee schedule under the Hague Convention of 5 October 1961, in force in China since 7 November 2023

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Licensed corporate domiciliation agent - registered office establishment (initial period)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg société de domiciliation licensed under the Law of 31 May 1999
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for regulated domiciliation services (EUR 1,500-2,500 per annum equivalent)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: RBE (Register of Beneficial Owners) UBO declaration filing
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory nil-fee filing under the amended Law of 13 January 2019

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Luxembourg Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended (Articles 1–11, 31–45, 103–116 for partnerships; SCSp-specific provisions introduced by the Law of 12 July 2013, Article 103-1 et seq.)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Association / Partnership Agreement and the RCS registration application filed electronically via Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) portal, followed by mandatory publication in the Recueil Electronique des Sociétés et Associations (RESA)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for an SCSp; partners may subscribe contributions in cash or in kind, with full subscription and no escrow account requirement; a bank account for contributions may still be required under the partnership agreement for practical purposes.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: (1) That the initial partners adopt the partnership agreement of the Société en Commandite Spéciale (SCSp) and declare the partnership formed. (2) That the partnership interests issued to each initial partner are hereby subscribed and accepted. (3) That the registered office of the partnership is established at [address], Luxembourg. (4) That [Name] is appointed as Manager and [Name] as authorised signatory. (5) That the Manager is instructed to open a bank account in the name of the partnership. (6) That all filings necessary for RCS registration, RESA publication, and statutory formalities be executed forthwith.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Draft and Notarise the Partnership Agreement and Related Corporate Documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg notary and legal counsel; RCS via Luxembourg Business Registers
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the SCSp partnership agreement, the list of initial partners with their respective contributions and profit-sharing ratios, and the registered office address. Have the agreement executed before a Luxembourg notary if real estate or certain in-kind contributions are involved; otherwise a private deed under private signature is permissible for a standard SCSp. Ensure all partner signatures are authenticated and each partner has provided certified identity documents and proof of address. Submit finalised corporate documents to legal counsel for pre-filing compliance review before proceeding with RCS registration.
required_dossiers: SCSp partnership agreement (drafted and signed by all partners)
Certified copies of identity documents of all partners
Proof of registered office address in Luxembourg
Declaration of no non-regulatory past or prior criminal record for the manager, if applicable
Bank reference letters or proof of contribution payment, as agreed in the partnership agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If RCS queries the partnership agreement or supporting documents, counsel shall revise the relevant clauses, obtain new signatures, and resubmit the corrected dossier within 5 working days; any notarial defects will be cured by re-execution before the notary.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File the Partnership Agreement and Register the SCSp with the RCS
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log in to the Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) online portal using an electronic signature. Complete the RCS registration form for a Special Limited Partnership (SCSp), upload the partnership agreement, identify the statutory manager and the registered office address, and pay the filing and publication fee. Submit the application electronically and retain the RCS acknowledgement receipt. After validation and publication in RESA, obtain the RCS registration extract.
required_dossiers: Completed RCS application form for SCSp registration
Signed partnership agreement in file format
Identity documents and powers of attorney of all partners and managers
Statement from the manager confirming domiciliation of the registered office
Payment confirmation for RCS filing and RESA publication fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If RCS issues a query or a rectification notice, legal counsel shall submit amended supporting documents or updated partnership agreement within 5 working days. If the proposed name is rejected due to conflict, a new name shall be reserved immediately and the registration resubmitted under the new name.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Open an Inward-Remittance Bank Account and Execute Tax Identity Formalities
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial banks in Luxembourg; Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) for tax number and VAT; RCS for registration of the tax identification number
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon issuance of the RCS registration extract, the manager shall open a Luxembourg bank account in the partnership's name. Provide the RCS extract, partnership agreement, partner identification, and beneficial ownership declarations to the bank's compliance team. Complete Form 510 for corporate tax registration and apply for a Luxembourg national identification number (NIF) at the RCS through the one-stop-shop procedure. If the partnership will undertake business subject to VAT, also file the VAT registration application with the AEDT.
required_dossiers: RCS registration extract (certified copy)
Certified partnership agreement
Beneficial ownership declaration for AML and tax purposes
Manager's and partners' passport copies and proof of address
Completed Luxembourg VAT registration form, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requests additional beneficial-ownership or source-of-funds information, collect and submit the requested documentation within 5 business days. Any delay in the issuance of the tax number shall be escalated to the RCS contact and the AEDT call centre, and provisional bank account instructions may be issued without tax identification where permitted by anti-money-laundering rules.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Adopt the Full Corporate Governance Framework by Written Resolution
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Partners' meeting / board of the SCSp as per the partnership agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The manager shall convene a partners' meeting or obtain a written circular resolution approving the corporate governance package. This package must include the first board resolution on appointees and mandate, internal rules on delegation of authority, the signing mandate for bank accounts, procedures for annual partner approvals, and a shareholder/partner register. Minutes of the meeting or the written resolution shall be dated and signed by all parties and retained in the corporate minute book.
required_dossiers: Notice of meeting or circular resolution process
Pro-forma first board resolution (covering subscription, registered office and officer appointments)
Partnership register or register of partners
Delegation of authority matrix and bank signing mandate
Minutes template for subsequent partner decisions
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a quorum or consent threshold is not reached, the manager shall convene a second meeting after 48 hours and adopt resolutions with the statutory majority permitted by the partnership agreement; alternatively, the written resolution can be circulated to partners for individual signature until unanimous consent is obtained.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execute the Statutory Publication and Final Registration Formalities
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – RCS and the Recueil Electronique des Sociétés et Associations (RESA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After internal approvals, the manager shall ensure that the full partnership agreement and the extracted registration data are submitted to the RCS for final publication in RESA. The filing must include the names of the general partner and manager, the registered office, and the object of the partnership. Confirm the RESA publication notice and obtain the final RCS certificate. Notify all business counterparties of the legal identifiers.
required_dossiers: Copy of the official RESA publication request
Final RCS registration extract
Confirmation of registered office from the domiciliation agent
Signed minutes of the governance resolutions approving final formalities
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If RCS rejects the publication submission due to incomplete partner details, correct the filing by submitting a rectification application electronically. Legal counsel shall follow up directly with the RCS publication desk to expedite re-publication and obtain a clean RESA excerpt.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Luxembourg Ministry of the Economy and/or the Ministry of Health (Direction de la Santé) – Division for Medical Devices and Ionising Radiation; operational permits coordinated by the Commune (municipality) where the facility is located
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Medical Device Manufacturing Establishment Licence / Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) Authorisation for manufacturers of Class IIa and IIb diagnostics devices under the EU Medical Device Regulation (Regulation (EU) 2017/745) and Luxembourg national implementing laws

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l'environnement, Luxembourg (Luxembourg Environmental Protection Agency)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category B – Environmental Impact Study / Class 4 Environmental Authorisation required for small and medium-scale industrial facilities involving electronics assembly, soldering, cleaning agents, or chemical storage; a full EIA Report is generally not required for low-threshold medical electronics assembly, but an environmental notification (déclaration) and an operational waste permit are mandatory.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater discharges must comply with Luxembourg Regulation on wastewater discharge and the Grand-Ducal Regulation of 16 May 2019 on water protection; volatile organic compounds (VOCs) from cleaning and soldering processes must be controlled below the national emissions thresholds set under the Industrial Emissions Directive (2010/75/EU), with batch testing and periodic air-emission measurement; all electronic waste, solder waste, and chemical containers must be disposed through approved waste handlers with consignment notes.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: The facility must secure a fire safety certificate from the Corps grand-ducal d'incendie et de secours (CGDIS), including the inspection of alarm systems, extinguishers, and emergency exits; structural load inspections and electrical installation clearance issued by an approved Luxembourg engineering bureau; occupational safety clearance by the Inspection du Travail et des Mines (ITM) covering workplace ergonomics, ionising-radiation exposure if applicable, electrical safety, and employee health surveillance.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) for direct income taxes; Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) for VAT and registration duties; digital access via guichet.public.lu and MyGuichet.lu
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign SCSp or its representative first registers with the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCS) through a notarized deed, then files the statutory registration forms 102/103 with the ACD and VAT form 640/641 with the AEDT. Non-EU resident investors may be required to appoint a Luxembourg tax representative for process service and VAT compliance. The competent authority issues a Luxembourg national tax identification number (matricule) and a separate VAT number upon acceptance of the application.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Luxembourg does not operate a US-style check-the-box election. The SCSp is statutorily fiscally transparent and is taxed at the level of its partners unless an optional election to be treated as a corporate taxpayer is available under Article 175 LIR and all partners consent. For cross-border hybrid arrangements, partners must document and file ATAD hybrid mismatch disclosures with the ACD, including Form 700 and supporting classification analysis.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (TVA) under the Luxembourg VAT Law of 12 February 1979, as amended
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 35,000 annual taxable turnover for the domestic small-business exemption; however, non-established foreign taxable persons making taxable supplies in Luxembourg must register for VAT from the first euro unless the EU one-stop-shop distance-selling or non-established trader thresholds apply.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Luxembourg does not currently mandate real-time fiscal clearance, digital stamping, or continuous transaction controls for B2B invoices. Electronic invoicing is permitted subject to partner consent and authenticity/integrity safeguards. B2G invoices must be submitted electronically through the national PEPPOL infrastructure to the Luxembourg Public Sector Integrated System. VAT records must be retained for six years and made available to the AEDT upon request.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods qualify for 0% VAT when physically dispatched or transported outside the European Union, supported by a validated customs export declaration, transport documents, commercial invoices, and proof that legal title and risk passed to a non-EU customer. Services qualify when supplied to a recipient established outside the EU and the effective use and enjoyment of the service occurs outside Luxembourg; where the recipient is a taxable person, the reverse-charge rules may apply instead of zero-rating.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Validated Customs Export Declaration (EX-A) or electronic export summary declaration
Bill of Lading / Air Waybill / CMR transport document evidencing departure from EU territory
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank SWIFT credit advice evidencing receipt of export proceeds
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Export zero-rating claims are subject to strict documentary verification. Inadequate or contradictory evidence within the statutory inspection window triggers reassessment at the 17% standard VAT rate plus late payment interest. Negligent insufficiency exposes the taxable person to administrative fines up to EUR 25,000; fraudulent zero-rating claims may be prosecuted under Article 42 of the Luxembourg VAT Law and result in criminal fines and imprisonment for the managing partners.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL), operating within the Eurosystem alongside the European Central Bank (ECB); banking supervision and AML/KYC enforcement are delegated to the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) under CSSF Circular 12/552 and the Law of 10 November 2009 on payment services, as amended; the BCL operates the T2/TARGET2 settlement infrastructure and the Luxembourg Interbank Payment System (LIPS).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The euro is fully convertible on both current and capital account. Luxembourg imposes no exchange-control approvals, no inward/outward capital declarations, and no restrictions on non-resident ownership of accounts. Liberalisation derives from Articles 63-66 TFEU (free movement of capital), Regulation (EU) 2018/1151 on European business statistics, and the EU Anti-Money Laundering framework. Profit remittance and SCSp distributions are unrestricted for both EU-resident and third-country LPs; because the SCSp is fiscally transparent (Luxembourg income tax law and the Law of 10 August 1915 on commercial companies, as amended by the Law of 12 July 2013), no Luxembourg withholding tax applies at partnership level unless the entity has elected taxable-corporate status, in which case standard corporate distribution rules would apply. The only practical obstacles for foreign LPs repatriating proceeds are bank-level KYC gates, EU/UN/OFAC sanctions screening, and BCL statistical reporting on cross-border flows above reporting thresholds; a GP distribution resolution and proof of Luxembourg tax/VAT good standing are required by banks in practice.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None applicable. Luxembourg maintains no mandatory surrender, conversion, or holding-period rules for export proceeds. The EUR-based SCSp may retain USD, CNY, or any freely convertible currency in onshore or offshore accounts, may net export receivables against import payables, and may extend open-account trade terms without central-bank consent. Residual obligations are limited to: (i) customs export declarations via the EU AES/ICS2 systems for the medical-scanner consignments; (ii) cross-border cash declarations above EUR 10,000 under Regulation (EU) 2018/1672; and (iii) crypto-asset transfer-data ('Travel Rule') transmission under Regulation (EU) 2023/1113, which does not apply to conventional wire transfers but is referenced for completeness.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational treasury current account opened in the SCSp's name (GP signatory), with optional segregated capital-contribution sub-account; separate collateral/escrow deposit for trade guarantees

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (BCEE / Spuerkeess)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational current account plus export-collections account and EUR/USD nostro-linked settlement
Operational account combined with documentary-credit desks (issuance, confirmation, negotiation) and short-term FX line
Operational treasury account with dedicated ISDA/forex derivatives line for hedging the USD export book
Secondary cash-clearing account for USD liquidity via the DB US/EU corridor; not essential for the core SCSp structure
Interest-bearing deposit account for excess EUR liquidity and term placements

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Quintet Private Bank (formerly KBL European Private Bankers)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Wealth-management custody account; unsuitable as primary treasury or trade-finance rail for an operating export entity

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: LOW-MEDIUM viability. Luxembourg law authorises Payment Institutions (Law of 10 November 2009) and Electronic Money Institutions (Law of 21 December 2012), both supervised by the CSSF; local EMIs such as Payconiq International and PPRO Financial can supply multi-currency IBANs, SEPA/T2 instant payments, and corporate cards. However, EMIs generally: (i) do not maintain correspondent banking for high-value USD MT103 clearing; (ii) cannot issue, advise, or settle commercial letters of credit (MT700/MT760) or documentary collections; and (iii) restrict physical-goods trade flows (medical scanners) under AML policies oriented to e-commerce/consumer payments. Offshore EMIs (UK, Singapore, UAE) cannot passport into Luxembourg post-Brexit without an EU branch or agent, so an unlicensed foreign EMI is not legally viable for the SCSp's bank-account duties under CSSF Circular 12/552. Recommended architecture: Tier-1 Luxembourg bank as primary treasury and LC rail; a CSSF- or other-EU-authorised EMI only for payroll card and small procurement spend, never for trade settlement.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote onboarding is legally permitted but institutionally constrained. CSSF Circular 12/552 mandates identification via: (a) physical interview with an authorised signatory; (b) eIDAS-qualified electronic signature (LuxTrust QES); or (c) bank-approved video identification with multi-factor authentication. In practice, Tier-1 banks require at least one in-person meeting of the General Partner's managing director and the 25%-plus beneficial owners at the bank's premises, at a Luxembourg notary, or at an acknowledged foreign branch, because the SCSp lacks separate legal personality and the mandate is exercised by the GP under Articles 27-1 et seq. of the Law of 10 August 1915. The bank will demand a notarised or apostilled signature book, the registered RCS excerpt, and the Limited Partnership Agreement. Realistic onboarding timeline is 6-10 weeks; fully digital onboarding is achievable only with CSSF-authorised digital lenders/neobanks or after an established relationship. The on-site interview should present the ISO 13485 manufacturing qualifications, CE-marking dossier under MDR (EU) 2017/745, and the export sales pipeline for the colour-Doppler ultrasound consoles.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: SCSp lacks separate legal personality, raising legal-capacity and instruction-authority objections during account opening and signature-card registration.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarised Limited Partnership Agreement (LPA); RCS excerpt for the SCSp and its General Partner; GP resolution appointing signatories and opening the treasury account; Luxembourg legal opinion confirming the SCSp's contractual-patrimony nature and the GP's binding authority; specimen signature card duly notarised or apostilled.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opaque limited-partner chain: any LP holding 25% or more (direct or indirect) that is itself a foreign entity, trust, or foundation triggers enhanced due diligence and UBO-identification failure risk.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete filing in the Luxembourg Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE) under the Law of 13 January 2019; annotated group structure chart down to natural-person UBOs; passport copies and proof of residential address for all material UBOs; tax-transparency ruling or reasoned Luxembourg tax opinion confirming the SCSp's pass-through status; declarations of ultimate ownership signed by each LP.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source-of-funds objection: initial capital injection from non-EEA LPs without audited track record or clear wealth-transmission trail.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Twelve months of LP bank statements; audited financial statements or certified tax returns of contributing LPs; signed statement of net wealth; notarised capital-contribution certificate; board/resolution of the LP authorising the contribution; annotated wire-trail explanation with all intermediate accounts disclosed.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Trade-based money-laundering scrutiny of high-value medical-imaging invoices to distributors or end-users in jurisdictions with perceived opacity in import licensing or beneficial ownership.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed purchase orders and distribution agreements; pro-forma invoices and final commercial invoices; EU customs export declarations (AES) and export licences from the Luxembourg Ministry of Health where applicable; CE certificate of conformity under MDR (EU) 2017/745; end-user certificates from consignees; bills of lading, packing lists, freight-forwarder records; bank-confirmed sanctions/PEP screening report on all counterparties (UN/EU/OFAC).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: FX-derivative capacity test: booking of forwards, swaps, or cross-currency hedges inside an unregulated SCSp with no standalone capital or income statement.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: GP-approved hedging policy resolution enumerating permissible instruments, tenors, and notional limits; USD net-exposure forecast derived from the ultrasound-console export pipeline; audited or reviewed financial statements of the SCSp; evidence of GP liability capital and any subordinated loan agreements; executed ISDA 2002 Master Agreement or bank standard FX master confirmation; legal opinion confirming the SCSp's capacity to enter derivative transactions for hedging (not speculation).

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound LP capital contributions are routed via SWIFT MT103 (non-EUR, typically USD) or SEPA/T2 credit transfer (EUR) to the SCSp's operational IBAN at the Luxembourg Tier-1 bank. Remittance information (field 70) must state 'SCSP CAPITAL CONTRIBUTION – [LPA reference and GP resolution date]' and, where requested by the receiving bank, the Luxembourg BCL statistical purpose code for direct-investment equity capital. No exchange-control permit or pre-clearance filing is required; however, the bank will block or delay the credit unless the KYC source-of-funds dossier is already complete. For USD injections, utilise the bank's New York/United States correspondent to avoid mid-tier clearing holds; for EUR, ensure the target IBAN is held in the SCSp's name (the GP is a signatory only, and the IBAN holder must be the partnership).
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Two parallel rails: (1) Pre-shipment deposits and milestone payments via SWIFT MT103 telegraphic transfers, with field 70 quoting the purchase order and underlying LC reference; (2) Post-shipment settlement via irrevocable, confirmed at-sight commercial letters of credit: the buyer's bank issues the LC to the Luxembourg advising/confirming bank through SWIFT MT700, and payment is made by MT103/MT202 upon presentation of compliant documents (commercial invoice, packing list, on-board bill of lading, certificate of origin, CE certificate, and insurance policy). For recurring low-ticket spare-part consignments, the SCSp may shift to open account with export-credit insurance (Euler Hermes/Coface) while still clearing through MT103 corporate e-banking. All outward wires pass the EU/OFAC sanctions filter; the Luxembourg bank debits the EUR account and applies same-day FX conversion at the negotiated spot margin.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: OTC EUR/USD spot transactions for conversion of export proceeds at commercial spot rates under the bank's standard FX regime
Vanilla EUR/USD FX forwards (tenor up to 12 months) documented under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement or the bank's local FX master confirmation
EUR/USD FX swaps (tom-next and spot-next) for intra-treasury liquidity positioning
EUR/USD cross-currency swaps for longer-term euro financing of the trade-receivables book, subject to GP hedging-policy approval
EUR/USD FX options and zero-cost collars to cap conversion risk on large LC invoices, with premium funding via the operating account

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on restricted or soft currencies (e.g., CNY, INR) where buyers in China or India require local-currency settlement; such NDFs are concluded with a counterparty outside the restricted market, settled in EUR/USD, and reported under EU EMIR obligations

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually within one month after the anniversary of the SCSp's initial RBE registration; confirmation is due in every year, even if no beneficial-owner change occurs
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to confirm constitutes a criminal offence under the UBO Law of 13 January 2019: fines from EUR 1,250 to EUR 1,250,000 per violation and, for intentional non-compliance, imprisonment; the LBR may block certified extracts and flag the file until regularized. No administrative strike-off applies to this filing alone.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounting records and financial statements for partner approval
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: General partner and limited partners of the SCSp (accounts are not filed with the RCSL)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Financial statements, when required by the limited partnership agreement, must be prepared and approved within six months after the SCSp's financial year-end; no public filing deadline applies to an SCSp
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to maintain proper accounting records violates the Law of 19 December 2002 and may trigger civil liability of the general partner and criminal fines; no RCSL strike-off arises because SCSp accounts are exempt from public filing.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: RCSL amendment filing for changes to registered particulars or the limited partnership agreement
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCSL) operated by LBR
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month after each event (change of general partner, registered office relocation, amendment of the partnership agreement, transfer of partnership interests); no fixed annual deadline if no change occurs
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filings are subject to RCSL late fees and potentially court fines; persistent failure to maintain accurate registration data or a valid registered office may lead to RCSL dissolution or administrative strike-off proceedings.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Statutory tax holidays or preferential deductions
